examples.japanese: {故人|こじん}のご{冥福|めいふく}をお{祈|いの}りします。
examples.english: I pray for the repose of the deceased.

examples.japanese: {故人|こじん}が{生前|せいぜん}{愛用|あいよう}していた{品々|しなじな}が、{遺族|いぞく}によって{大切|たいせつ}に{保管|ほかん}されている。
examples.english: The items the deceased cherished during their lifetime are being carefully preserved by the bereaved family.

notes:
{故人|こじん} is a respectful term for a deceased person.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {故人|こじん}を{偲|しの}ぶ (remember the deceased)
- {故人|こじん}の{遺志|いし} (the deceased's wishes)
- {故人|こじん}の{冥福|めいふく}を{祈|いの}る (pray for their soul)

NOTE: Different from {個人|こじん} (individual) - same reading but different meaning.

RELATED:
- {亡|な}くなった{人|ひと} (person who passed away - less formal)
- {遺族|いぞく} (bereaved family)
